items.q: What does one mole of a substance contain?
options: One gram of the substance, whatever it is made of
The number of atoms in one molecule of the substance
6.022 × 10²³ of the particles named, such as atoms or molecules
Enough of the substance to fill a 1-liter container

items.q: How many moles of aluminum atoms are in Sample 1?

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied the mass by the molar mass. Divide, so that grams cancel and moles are left.

items.q: Which sample contains the greatest number of atoms in total?
options: Sample 3, the water
Sample 2, the copper
Sample 4, the ethanol
Sample 5, the sucrose

items.q: How many hydrogen atoms are in Sample 4?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the number of ethanol molecules. Each molecule has 6 hydrogen atoms, so multiply by 6.

items.q: Sample 2 has about 9.4 times the mass of Sample 1 but only about 4.0 times as many atoms. Which statement explains this?
options: Copper atoms are packed closer together, so more fit in the sample
Each copper atom has about 2.4 times the mass of an aluminum atom
A mole of copper contains more atoms than a mole of aluminum
The copper mass has fewer significant figures, which lowers its count

items.q: Which box holds the greatest mass of gas?
options: Box A, because its particles contain the most atoms
Box B, because it holds as many particles as Box A and each is heavier
The three boxes have equal masses
Box C, with 3 carbon dioxide molecules

items.q: Boxes A and B hold the same number of particles. How do their masses compare, and why?
options: Box B is heavier, because a neon atom has more mass than a water molecule
They have equal masses, because they hold equal numbers of particles
Box A is heavier, because each water molecule has three atoms
Box A is heavier, because water is a compound and neon is an element

items.q: Which box contains the greatest number of atoms?
options: Box B
Box C
Box A
Boxes A and B, which tie

items.q: Suppose each particle drawn stands for 0.100 mol of that substance. What mass of carbon dioxide does Box C represent?

mistakes.why: Value: that is one particle's worth. Box C has 3 particles, so 0.300 mol.
Value: you divided moles by molar mass. Multiply: mol × g/mol = g.
Value: you counted atoms (9) instead of molecules (3). Each CO₂ molecule is one particle of carbon dioxide.

items.q: What is the molar mass of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃? Use Ca 40.08, C 12.01, O 16.00.

mistakes.why: Value: the subscript 3 applies to oxygen. Count three O atoms: 3 × 16.00 = 48.00.

items.q: What is the mass of 0.0250 mol of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆ (molar mass 180.16 g/mol)?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided by the molar mass. From moles to grams, multiply by g/mol.

items.q: What is the mass, in grams, of a single water molecule (18.02 g/mol)?

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied by Avogadro's number. One molecule is a tiny fraction of a mole, so divide.

items.q: A flask holds 1.0 g of hydrogen gas, H₂, and another holds 1.0 g of oxygen gas, O₂. Which statement is correct?
options: Both flasks hold the same number of molecules, since the masses match
The hydrogen flask holds about 16 times as many molecules
The oxygen flask holds more molecules, since oxygen atoms are larger
The flasks need their volumes before they can be compared

items.q: One molecule of ethanol has a mass of 46.07 amu. What is the mass of one mole of ethanol molecules?
Which samples contain 1.00 mol of the particles named? Select all that apply.
options: 55.85 g of iron atoms (Fe, 55.85 g/mol)
1.00 g of hydrogen gas, counted as H₂ molecules
16.00 g of oxygen gas, counted as O₂ molecules
32.00 g of oxygen gas, counted as O₂ molecules
6.022 × 10²² water molecules

items.q: Four flasks each hold 1.0 g of a gas. Put them in order from the fewest moles to the most.
options: CO₂ (44.01 g/mol)
O₂ (32.00 g/mol)
CH₄ (16.04 g/mol)
H₂ (2.016 g/mol)

items.q: A 50.0 g sample of water (18.02 g/mol) is replaced by 50.0 g of methane, CH₄ (16.04 g/mol). Predict how each quantity changes.
A student reports that 2.0 g of helium (4.003 g/mol) contains 4.8 × 10²⁴ atoms. Which quick check shows the answer is wrong?
options: 2.0 g is about half a mole, so it should be about 3 × 10²³ atoms
Helium is a gas, so it has fewer atoms than a solid of the same mass
A count of atoms is at most 6.022 × 10²³, one mole
The answer should have units of grams, not atoms

items.q: What do all atoms of one element have in common?
options: The same number of neutrons
The same mass number
The same number of protons
The same mass, to the nearest 0.001 amu

items.q: An atom of chlorine has 17 protons and 20 neutrons. What is its mass number?
How many neutrons are in an atom of iron-56? Iron has atomic number 26.

mistakes.why: Value: you added the numbers. The mass number already includes the protons, so subtract: 56 − 26.

items.q: How many isotopes of this element does the spectrum show?
options: One, since the sample is a pure element
Three
Twenty-five, the middle mass
Two, since the smaller peaks count as one

items.q: Calculate the average atomic mass of the element from the spectrum.

mistakes.why: Value: you took a simple average of the three masses. Weight each mass by its abundance: most atoms are the light isotope.
Value: you used percents, not fractions. Divide each abundance by 100 (78.99% is 0.7899).

items.q: Which element is this, and what evidence supports the claim?
options: Sodium, because the tallest peak is near 23
Chromium, because three isotopes add to a mass near 75
Aluminum, because 24 + 25 + 26 is close to 27 times 3
Magnesium, whose atomic mass on the periodic table is 24.31

items.q: Why is the average atomic mass much closer to 24 than to 25?
options: About 79% of the atoms are the isotope of mass 24
The isotope of mass 24 has the most protons
Heavier isotopes are not counted in the average
The spectrometer detects lighter ions more easily

items.q: How do the atoms that make the peak at m/z = 26 differ from those at m/z = 24?
options: They have two more protons
They have two more electrons
They have two more neutrons
They carry a charge of 2+ instead of 1+

items.q: Calculate the average atomic mass of gallium from the table.

mistakes.why: Value: that is a simple average. Gallium-69 is more common, so weight each mass by its abundance.

items.q: Boron's average atomic mass is 10.81 amu. Using the table, what percentage of boron atoms are boron-11?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the boron-10 share. The average (10.81) is closer to 11, so most atoms are boron-11.

items.q: A student says chlorine's mass spectrum would show one peak at 35.45, the atomic mass on the periodic table. Which response is correct?
options: Yes, because the spectrometer reports the average mass of the atoms in the sample
No; the spectrum shows peaks at 35 and 37 of equal height
No; it shows one peak at 36, halfway between the isotopes
No; it shows peaks near 35 and 37, the first about three times taller

items.q: Gallium's average atomic mass, 69.72 amu, falls between its two isotope masses. Which claim about the data is supported?
options: A third gallium isotope with a mass near 69.7 is likely
The average is nearer 69 because gallium-69 is the more common isotope
Gallium-71 has more protons than gallium-69
The abundances are probably wrong, since the mass is below the midpoint

items.q: An atom of oxygen gains two electrons. What does it become?
options: A cation with a 2+ charge
An anion with a 2− charge
An isotope of oxygen with a mass two units higher
An atom of neon, which has two more electrons

items.q: Which particles have more protons than electrons? Select all that apply.
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
O²⁻
Ne

items.q: In a mass spectrometer, why are the atoms first turned into ions?
options: The fields that steer and sort particles act on charged particles
Removing an electron makes each atom lighter, so the peaks spread out
Ions of different isotopes differ in protons, which the detector counts
Neutral atoms of one element share one mass, so they need no sorting

items.q: Which pair are isotopes of each other?
options: ⁴⁰Ar and ⁴⁰Ca
¹⁶O and ¹⁶O²⁻
²⁸Si and ³⁰Si
¹²C and ¹⁴N

items.q: What is the mass percent of magnesium in Group 1's product?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the oxygen share. Use the mass of magnesium on top.
Value: divide by the mass of the whole product (2.016 g), not by the oxygen alone.

items.q: Which conclusion do the three groups' results support?
options: Magnesium oxide is about 60.3% magnesium by mass in each sample
Larger samples of magnesium oxide contain a larger percent of magnesium
Magnesium and oxygen combine in a 1 : 1 ratio by mass
The groups made different compounds, since their product masses differ

items.q: Using Group 2's data, what is the empirical formula of magnesium oxide?
options: Mg₃O₂
MgO₂
Mg₂O
MgO

items.q: Based on the groups' results, what mass of magnesium is in 12.5 g of magnesium oxide?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the oxygen in the sample. Use the magnesium fraction, 0.6032.
Value: you divided by the fraction. The part is the whole times the fraction.

items.q: A fourth group's product had a magnesium mass percent of 66%. Which error best explains this result?
options: The group used more magnesium than the other groups
Some magnesium did not react, so the product was too light
The product absorbed water from the air after heating
The balance read each mass 0.05 g too high

items.q: What is the empirical formula of the compound?
options: C₄₀H₇O₅₃
C₃H₇O₃
C₆H₁₂O₆
CH₂O

items.q: What is the molar mass of the empirical formula CH₂O (one C, two H and one O)?

C₁₂H₂₄O₁₂
C₆H₁₂O₆
C₃H₆O₃

items.q: Another compound has the same mass percents (40.00% C, 6.71% H, 53.29% O) but a molar mass of 60.05 g/mol. Which statement is correct?
options: It is the same compound, because the mass percents match
The data are wrong, since two compounds do not share mass percents
Its empirical formula is also CH₂O, and its molecular formula is C₂H₄O₂
Its molecular formula is CH₂O, since 60.05 is close to 30.03

items.q: Urea, CH₄N₂O, is used as a fertilizer. What is the mass percent of nitrogen in urea? (C 12.01, H 1.008, N 14.01, O 16.00)

mistakes.why: Value: urea has two N atoms. Use 2 × 14.01 for the nitrogen mass.

items.q: A 2.233 g sample of iron reacts with oxygen to make 3.193 g of an iron oxide. What is the empirical formula of the oxide? (Fe 55.85, O 16.00)

FeO₂
Fe₃O₂
Fe₂O₃

items.q: Put the steps for finding an empirical formula from mass percents in order.
options: Assume a 100 g sample so each percent becomes grams
Divide each mass by its molar mass to get moles
Divide every mole value by the smallest one
Multiply by a small whole number if any ratio is not close to whole
Write the formula with the whole-number ratios as subscripts

items.q: A student finds that elements X and Y are present in moles in the ratio 1 : 1.33 and writes the formula XY. What should the student have done?
options: Round 1.33 to 1, so XY is correct
Multiply both by 3 to get 3 : 4, so X₃Y₄
Multiply both by 2 to get 2 : 2.66, so X₂Y₃
Divide both by 1.33 to get 0.75 : 1, then round to XY

items.q: A compound of only carbon and hydrogen has the empirical formula CH₂ (14.03 g/mol). Which could be its molecular formula? Select all that apply.
options: C₂H₄
C₃H₆
CH₄
C₂H₆

items.q: Water and hydrogen peroxide both contain only hydrogen and oxygen. Water is 11.2% H by mass; hydrogen peroxide is 5.93% H. Which explains the difference?
options: They are different compounds, H₂O and H₂O₂, with different atom ratios
Hydrogen peroxide samples were less pure than the water samples
The law of definite proportions says compounds of two elements share a composition
Hydrogen atoms in the peroxide are lighter than the hydrogen atoms in water

items.q: A compound is 26.58% K, 35.35% Cr and 38.07% O by mass. What is its empirical formula? (K 39.10, Cr 52.00, O 16.00)

mistakes.why: Value: you counted atoms (8 N out of 13). The question asks for particles: 4 N₂ molecules out of 7.

Box Z holds H₂O, O₂ and H₂: three kinds of particle
Box Z has an odd number of hydrogen atoms, so it is a mixture

What is the percent purity (percent CaCO₃ by mass) of Brand P's tablet?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the percent calcium in the tablet. Convert the calcium to CaCO₃ first, then divide by the tablet mass.

items.q: Which brand's tablet contains the most filler?

Brand P
Brand R

items.q: Suppose some of the filler in a tablet also contained calcium. How would the calculated purity compare with the true purity?

Unchanged, since the CaCO₃ itself is weighed
Too high, since extra calcium is counted as CaCO₃
It could no longer be calculated from these data

items.q: A label claims Brand Q is "99% pure calcium carbonate." Do the data support the claim?
options: Yes: 0.4955 g Ca is 1.237 g CaCO₃, 99.0% of 1.250 g
No: the tablet is 39.6% calcium, far below 99%
No: a 1.250 g tablet would need 1.24 g of calcium
Yes: the brands' tablets have equal masses, so equal purity

Pure water
Sand in water
Salt water, the same throughout

options: Both are mixtures, because both contain two elements
Sample 1 is likely a compound; Sample 2, an uneven mixture
Both are compounds, because both contain iron and sulfur
Sample 2 is likely a compound because its iron content is lower

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied by the fraction. The salt is the whole and chlorine the part, so divide by 0.6066.

items.q: Which observations are at the macroscopic level? Select all that apply.

The sample has a mass of 2.48 g
Each particle holds one Fe and one S atom
Oxygen molecules are made of two atoms

items.q: A student adds more sugar to a 5.00 g mixture of salt and sugar. Predict how each quantity changes.

variables.name: Mass of chlorine in the sample
Mass percent of chlorine in the sample
Mass percent of chlorine in the salt itself

Look at it closely to check that it is evenly white

items.q: How many valence electrons does an atom of phosphorus, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³, have?

Value: that is all the electrons. Valence electrons are only those in the outermost shell.

items.q: It takes more energy to remove the outermost electron from lithium than from sodium. Which explanation is best?
options: Sodium is a bigger atom, so it has a weaker hold on each of its electrons
Lithium has fewer protons, so it holds its electron more tightly
Sodium's valence electron is in shell 3, farther out, behind 10 core electrons
Sodium has more mass, which makes its electrons easier to remove

items.q: Neon has fewer protons than sodium, yet removing neon's outermost electron takes about four times as much energy. Which explanation fits Coulomb's law?
options: Neon's outer electron is in shell 2, closer, behind just 2 core electrons
Neon is a gas, and electrons are harder to remove from gases
Neon has a full shell, which wants to stay full
Sodium has more electrons, so it can spare one more easily

items.q: How many core electrons does sodium have?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the valence electron. Core electrons are the inner ones, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶.

items.q: Which statements about the three atoms are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Lithium and sodium each have one valence electron
Neon's valence shell is n = 2
Sodium's valence electron is in a p subshell
Lithium has more core electrons than sodium

3s
3p

3d
4p

variables.name: Energy needed to remove that electron

items.q: How many electrons can one p subshell hold?

2s

items.q: Why is the 1s peak at a far higher binding energy than any other peak?
options: 1s electrons have more charge than the other electrons
The 1s subshell holds the fewest electrons, so each is held more tightly
1s electrons are the valence electrons, which are the most tightly held
They are closest to the nucleus, with no shielding electrons

items.q: Which electrons in this atom are its valence electrons?
options: The electrons in the tallest peak
Those in the two lowest-energy peaks
The electrons in the peak with the highest binding energy
The six electrons at 10.3 MJ/mol and the two at 15.1 MJ/mol

items.q: Every peak in magnesium's spectrum is at a higher binding energy than the matching peak for sodium. Which explanation is best?
options: Magnesium has more electrons, which pull each other closer to the nucleus
Its extra proton pulls harder on each subshell
Magnesium atoms are larger, so their electrons are held more tightly
Magnesium's electrons are in higher shells than sodium's

items.q: How do the lowest-energy peaks of the two spectra differ in height?
options: They are the same height, since both are 3s peaks
Sodium's is taller, since sodium loses its electron more easily
Magnesium's is six times as tall, like its 2p peak
Magnesium's is twice as tall: 3s² against 3s¹

items.q: Using the spectrum, what is the minimum energy needed to remove one electron from one mole of gaseous sodium atoms, in kJ/mol?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the 1s electron, the hardest to remove. The minimum energy removes the outermost (3s) electron.

items.q: A student predicts that aluminum (13 protons, [Ne] 3s² 3p¹) will have a new small peak at a binding energy just above magnesium's 3s peak. What is wrong with the prediction?
options: Aluminum should have no new peak, since it fills the same subshells as magnesium
The new peak should be 6 electrons tall, since it is a p subshell
The new 3p peak belongs below aluminum's 3s peak, at lower binding energy
The new peak should be at a higher energy than aluminum's 1s peak

items.q: In photoelectron spectroscopy, what does the height of a peak tell you?
options: How tightly those electrons are held
The number of protons in the atom
The number of electrons in the subshell
Which shell the electrons are in

options: Fluorine
Phosphorus
Boron
Neon

items.q: Which statements about photoelectron spectra are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Each peak corresponds to one subshell
A larger nuclear charge shifts matching peaks to lower binding energy
Electrons in a 2p subshell have a higher binding energy than those in 2s
The peak with the lowest binding energy belongs to a core electron

items.q: Put the subshells of argon (1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶) in order of binding energy, highest first.
options: 1s
2s
2p
3s
3p

items.q: Compare the spectrum of potassium (19 protons, [Ar] 4s¹) with that of argon (18 protons). Predict the change from argon to potassium.
In a photoelectron spectrometer, how is the binding energy of an electron found?
options: By weighing the atom before and after the electron leaves
By counting how many electrons leave each second
From the size of the atom measured under a microscope
Light energy minus the ejected electron's energy of motion

items.q: Two peaks in one atom's spectrum are at 1.46 MJ/mol and 0.79 MJ/mol, with equal heights. Which statement is supported?
options: The electrons at 1.46 MJ/mol are held more tightly
The electrons at 0.79 MJ/mol are closer to the nucleus
The peak at 0.79 MJ/mol has more electrons
Both peaks belong to one subshell

items.q: How many valence electrons does X have, and what is the evidence?
options: Five: five ionization energies are listed
Two: the energy roughly triples from the 1st to the 2nd
Three: the energy jumps fourfold at the 4th electron
Four: the 4th energy is the largest one in the outer shell

items.q: Which element is X?
options: Aluminum
Magnesium
Phosphorus
Boron

items.q: Why is the 4th ionization energy so much larger than the 3rd?
options: The ion X³⁺ has a full outer shell, which it wants to keep
The 4th electron has a larger charge than the first three
The nucleus gains protons as electrons are removed
The 4th electron is in shell 2, closer and less shielded

items.q: What is the total energy needed to remove all the valence electrons from one mole of gaseous X atoms?

mistakes.why: Value: you added all five energies. Only the first three electrons are valence electrons.
Value: that is only the 3rd electron. Add the energies for all three valence electrons.

items.q: Each successive ionization energy of X is larger than the one before. Why?
options: Each electron removed is closer to the nucleus than the one before
Each comes from an ion that is more positive than before
The atom gains mass after each electron is removed
Later electrons are in s subshells, which are held more tightly

items.q: Which explanation accounts for the decrease in atomic radius from Na to Cl?
options: Atoms with more electrons pack their electrons more tightly
Each element across the period fills a new, smaller shell
Heavier atoms are denser and so take up less space
Protons rise while the shell and core electrons stay the same

items.q: Al has a lower first ionization energy than Mg, against the trend. Which explanation is best?
options: Al loses a 3p electron, which is higher in energy than 3s
Al has more protons, so it holds its electrons less tightly
Mg has a full 3s subshell, which it wants to keep
Al is a larger atom than Mg

items.q: Which element in the table attracts shared electrons most strongly?
options: Na
S
Cl
P

items.q: Which claim about the trends in the table is supported by the data?
options: First ionization energy rises at each step across the period
Atomic radius increases with the number of protons
As radius decreases, electronegativity increases
Electronegativity is unrelated to atomic radius

items.q: Why is the first ionization energy of potassium lower than that of sodium?
options: K's valence electron is farther out and more shielded
K has more protons, which push the electron away
K has more mass, so its electron moves faster
K is a metal and Na is not

items.q: How does each ion's radius compare with the radius of its own atom?
options: Na⁺ is larger than Na, and Cl⁻ is smaller than Cl
Na⁺ is larger than Na, and Cl⁻ is larger than Cl
Na⁺ is smaller than Na, and Cl⁻ is smaller than Cl
Na⁺ is smaller than Na, and Cl⁻ is larger than Cl

items.q: O²⁻, F⁻ and Na⁺ each have 10 electrons. Which is smallest, and why?
options: O²⁻, because it has the smallest atomic number
Na⁺, since 11 protons pull on the same 10 electrons
F⁻, because it is in the middle of the three
They are the same size, since they have the same electrons

items.q: Moving down group 2 from magnesium to calcium, predict how each quantity changes.
Fluorine is more electronegative than iodine. Which statements correctly help explain this? Select all that apply.
options: Fluorine's valence electrons are in shell 2, much closer to the nucleus
Iodine's valence electrons are shielded by many more core electrons
Iodine has more protons, so it attracts electrons more strongly
Fluorine has a larger mass than iodine

items.q: Where on the periodic table are the metals?
options: On the left and in the middle
In the top right corner of the table
In group 18, the last column
Along the staircase line

Box 3
Box 1
Boxes 1 and 3 both could

items.q: Which formula matches Box 3?
options: MgO: a 2+ cation and a 2− anion, 1 : 1
Mg₂O₂: two of each ion in each formula
NaCl: a 1+ cation and a 1− anion, 1 : 1
MgCl₂: twice as many anions as cations

items.q: Why does every box contain cations and anions in the ratio it does?
options: Each cation can touch two anions at a time
Larger ions are outnumbered by smaller ones
The ions are counted by mass, so heavier ions appear less often
The charges cancel, so each solid is neutral

options: Nitrogen forms no ions, so it does not belong in the box
Its charges do not cancel; Ca₃N₂ has 3 Ca²⁺ per 2 N³⁻
The ratio should be 2 Ca²⁺ to 3 N³⁻, Ca₂N₃
Calcium ions should carry a 1+ charge
